Objective Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disease characterized by initial involvement of the olfactory bulb/amygdala or autonomic nerves followed by nigral degeneration. Although autonomic innervation strictly regulates multiorgan systems, including endocrine functions, circulation, and digestion, how dysautonomia in PD affects systemic metabolism has not been identified. In this study, we tried to estimate the pathogenic linkage of PD by nuclear medicine techniques, trans‐omic analysis of blood samples, and cultured cell experiments. Methods Thyroid mediastinum ratio of 123 I‐metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy was measured in 1,158 patients with PD. Furthermore, serum exosome miRNA transcriptome analysis and plasma metabolome analysis followed by trans‐omic analysis were performed in patients with de novo PD and age‐matched healthy control persons. Additionally, thyroid hormone was administered to skeletal muscle and liver derived cells to evaluate the effect of hypothyroidism for these organs. Results Sympathetic denervation of thyroid correlating with its cardiac denervation was confirmed in 1,158 patients with PD by MIBG scintigraphy. Among patients with drug‐naïve PD, comprehensive metabolome analysis revealed decreased levels of thyroxine and insufficient fatty acid β‐oxidation, which positively correlate with one another. Likewise, both plasma metabolome data and transcriptome data of circulating exosomal miRNAs, revealed specific enrichment of the peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor (PPARα) axis. Finally, association of thyroid hormone with PPARα‐dependent β‐oxidation regulation was confirmed by in vitro experiments. Interpretation Our findings suggest that interorgan communications between the thyroid and liver are disorganized in the early stage of PD, which would be a sensitive diagnostic biomarker for PD. Hormones, cytokines, growth factors, and immunoglobulins connect isolated organs throughout the body to regulate whole‐body metabolism. 9 Although metabolic changes in amino acids, kynurenine, caffeine, fatty acids (FAs), and polyamines in the serum/plasma of patients with PD have been identified by us and others, those arising from dysautonomia remain unclear. 10 , 11 , 12 The thyroid is one of the most important organs regulating metabolism of the brain, white fat, brown fat, skeletal muscles, and liver, mainly under control of the hypothalamus‐pituitary‐thyroid axis. 13 In addition, use of animal models has delineated a functional role for sympathetic innervation on thyroid hormone secretion. 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 In humans, blood supplied from the intrathyroidal artery is regulated by sympathetic nerves, mainly from the cervical ganglia along the artery. 13 Sympathetic innervation of the thyroid in healthy humans was confirmed by 6‐ 18 F‐fluorodopamine imaging with/without desipramine, an inhibitor of serotonin/noradrenaline uptake. 18 In patients with PD, significant decreases of MIBG or 6‐ 18 F‐fluorodopamine uptake in the thyroid have been identified. 18 , 19 , 20 Horsager et al found that postganglionic autonomic denervation is initiated from celiac or mesenteric ganglions and retrogradely expanded to cervical ganglia in one subtype of PD. 21 Because pharmacologic doses of dopamine, glucocorticoids, and somatostatin suppress thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), 22 it remains unclear how thyroid function affects downstream target organs, such as skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, and liver in PD treated with/without L‐DOPA and/or dopamine agonists. Here, we report sympathetic denervation of the thyroid by cardiac MIBG scintigraphy in patients with PD, especially those with constipation, that correlated with cardiac denervation and nigral dopamine degeneration. Moreover, we identified suppression of FA β‐oxidation and its positive correlation with thyroxine levels in patients with de novo PD. To investigate interorgan communication, we performed transcriptome analysis of circulating serum exosomal miRNAs, which may serve as mediators among organs and appropriate diagnostic biomarkers for several diseases compared with non‐exosomal miRNAs. 23 , 24 , 25 Based on these assays, the peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor (PPARα) axis was enriched. Finally, we confirmed an association between thyroid hormone and the PPARα pathway in the liver using cultured human cell lines, proposing inter‐tissue communication in early PD.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated systemic metabolic alterations in early Parkinson's disease (PD), focusing on the thyroid-liver axis, dysautonomia, and fatty acid beta-oxidation. It utilized nuclear medicine techniques (MIBG scintigraphy, DaT-SPECT) in 1,158 PD patients, combined with trans-omic analyses (serum exosome miRNA transcriptome and plasma metabolome) in de novo PD patients, and in vitro cell experiments. Key findings include sympathetic denervation of the thyroid and heart correlating with disease severity, decreased thyroxine levels, insufficient fatty acid β-oxidation, and enrichment of the PPARα axis. The research identified significantly altered exosomal miRNAs and demonstrated the association of thyroid hormone with PPARα-dependent β-oxidation regulation and enhanced mitochondrial function in muscle cells, suggesting disorganized interorgan communication as a sensitive diagnostic biomarker.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Diagnostic Study of Parkinson's Disease Pathophysiology; In vitro Hormonal Stimulation and RNA-interference.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved observational investigation and diagnostic imaging (MIBG scintigraphy, 123I-ioflupane-dopamine transporter (DaT)-SPECT) on Parkinson's disease patients; no therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were conducted on human subjects. For mechanistic insights, in vitro experiments were performed on cultured HepG2 and primary human skeletal myotubular cells, stimulated with 100 nM 3,3′,5-triiodo-L-thyronine (T3). siRNA oligonucleotides were transfected into HepG2 cells and myotubes, with experiments conducted 48 hours post-transfection. While T3 treatment showed an 'almost dose-dependent' effect on CPT1A expression in HepG2 cells, specific concentrations for siRNA knockdown were not provided, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the overall observational study or the siRNA interventions.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Sympathetic Innervation Status (assessed by MIBG uptake, H/M ratios, T/M ratios, and 6-18F-fluorodopamine uptake)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Nuclear medicine imaging (123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy, 6-18F-fluorodopamine imaging), Imaging ratio (indicator of sympathetic innervation)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease in MIBG uptake in the thyroid and cardiac tissue in 1,158 PD patients, correlating with cardiac denervation and disease severity. Early H/M ratios were significantly decreased in PD patients (with/without constipation) and correlated negatively with H&Y stage. Early T/M ratios were significantly decreased in PD patients (especially with constipation), correlated negatively with H&Y stage, and positively with H/M ratios and thyroxine levels. Decreased ventricular 6-18F-fluorodopamine uptake was observed in 100% of PD patients with orthostatic hypotension and 47.8% without.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the integrity and density of postganglionic sympathetic innervation, crucial for regulating multiorgan systems and hormone secretion.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early Parkinson's disease, particularly in patients with constipation or orthostatic hypotension.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disorganized interorgan communication (thyroid-liver axis), a systemic pattern of neurodegeneration, and serves as a sensitive diagnostic biomarker for early PD.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased levels of thyroxine in drug-naïve and de novo PD patients (p=0.0066), even after adjusting for confounders. Modestly decreased total serum thyroid hormone levels. Thyroxine positively correlated with long-chain acylcarnitines (LC-ACs) and negatively with long-chain fatty acids (LC-FAs). Significantly correlated with early H/M ratio (r=0.635, p=0.0359) and early T/M ratio (r=0.828, p=0.0009). Decreasing thyroid hormone levels are suggested to induce systemic insults.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Thyroid hormone, essential for regulating whole-body metabolism, including fatty acid beta-oxidation, energy homeostasis, and hepatic lipid metabolism, with neuroprotective effects.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Drug-naïve and de novo Parkinson's disease, associated with fatty acid beta-oxidation insufficiency and thyroid-liver interorgan discoordination.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disrupted thyroid-liver axis, systemic metabolic alteration, and hypothyroidism in early PD, which can induce systemic and brain insults; plays a role in insufficient FA beta-oxidation.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Serum (decreased levels in patients); treatment applied to human HepG2 cells and primary human skeletal myotubular cells
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Hormone concentration (in vivo), Hormone treatment (in vitro)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased (CPT1A gene, PGC1α gene, mitochondrial respiration, ATP production); decreased (free FAs in cell culture).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum levels were modestly decreased in de novo PD patients. In HepG2 cells, T3 increased CPT1A gene expression in an almost dose-dependent manner and decreased free FAs in the culture medium. In human skeletal myotubular cells, T3 increased PGC1α gene expression and significantly enhanced mitochondrial basal respiration and ATP production.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Active form of thyroid hormone; regulates metabolism, including fatty acid metabolism (via PPARα-mediated CPT1 expression) and energy metabolism (via PGC1α).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: De novo Parkinson's disease (in vivo); in vitro study using HepG2 cells and human skeletal myotubular cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Modestly decreased serum levels in de novo PD indicate hypothyroidism. In vitro, T3 regulates PPARα-mediated CPT1 expression and enhances mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle, indicating improved energy metabolism.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Fatty Acid Metabolites (Long-chain Fatty Acids (LC-FAs), Long-chain Acylcarnitines (LC-ACs), and AC(16:0)/FA(16:0) ratio)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Systemic (inferred from plasma/serum metabolome), Plasma, Serum, culture medium of HepG2 cells (free FAs)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Metabolite concentration, Metabolic process activity, Metabolite ratio

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (insufficient beta-oxidation); higher (LC-FAs); lower (LC-ACs); positively correlated (AC(16:0) and AC(16:0)/FA(16:0) ratio with thyroxine and T/M ratio)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Insufficient fatty acid β-oxidation was revealed in drug-naïve PD patients. Significant increases in 11 LC-FAs and decreases in 12 LC-ACs were observed in PD patients, even after adjusting for confounders. LC-FAs were inversely correlated with thyroxine, while LC-ACs were positively correlated. Levels of AC(16:0) and AC(16:0)/FA(16:0) ratio positively correlated with thyroxine. Early T/M ratios positively correlated with AC(16:0)/FA(16:0) ratio. T3 treatment decreased free FAs in HepG2 cell culture medium.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Energy metabolism, involving the breakdown of fatty acids for energy production, and transport of fatty acids into mitochondria.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Drug-naïve and de novo Parkinson's disease; T3 treatment in HepG2 cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic metabolic dysregulation and fatty acid beta-oxidation insufficiency in early PD, potentially linked to dysregulated thyroid function and disorganized thyroid-liver axis.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Circulating serum exosomes (miRNA transcriptome) and plasma (metabolome), Systemic (derived from trans-omics), HepG2 cells and human skeletal myotubular cells
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene expression/pathway enrichment, Signaling pathway activity, Gene expression (via siRNA knockdown)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Specific enrichment of the PPARα axis in both plasma metabolome and exosomal miRNA transcriptome data in de novo PD. Predicted to be significantly altered, contributing to metabolomic and transcriptomic changes, and enriched with suppressed fatty acid β-oxidation. siRNA knockdown of PPARα partially but significantly suppressed CPT1A mRNA and protein levels in T3-treated cells. Reducing PPARα signaling is associated with inducing systemic insults.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates fatty acid metabolism, including β-oxidation, and modulates hepatic lipid metabolism by thyroid hormones; involved in neuroprotection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early/de novo Parkinson's disease (without medication) via trans-omics analysis; T3 treatment and siRNA knockdown in human HepG2 cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Implicated in disorganized interorgan communications (thyroid-PPARα-liver axis) and suppressed FA beta-oxidation in early PD; dysregulation contributes to systemic metabolic insults.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: miRNA expression level, Gene transcript level (miRNA abundance)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 101 upregulated miRNAs (p < 0.05) and 141 significantly altered miRNAs identified in de novo PD patients. Pathway enrichment analysis indicated alterations in FA biosynthesis and thyroid signaling. Specific examples include hsa-miR-223-5p, miR-652-3p, hsa-miR-181c-5p, hsa-miR-1,273h-5p, hsa-miR-199b-5p, and miR-338-3p, with consistent directions observed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulate gene expression, involved in inter-tissue communication and metabolic pathways (e.g., Fatty acid biosynthesis, Thyroid hormone signaling pathway).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential diagnostic or prognostic markers for de novo PD; reliably reflect the state of parental cells and can affect distant organs; indicate alterations consistent with insufficient FA β-oxidation and declined thyroid function in PD.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain (dopamine transporter availability via SPECT imaging)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Imaging ratio (indicator of dopamine transporter availability)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in patients with PD compared with the non-PD group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures dopamine transporter availability in the brain, reflecting dopaminergic neuronal integrity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Consistent with previous reports for Parkinson's Disease diagnosis/pathology.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased (by T3); decreased (in thyroid hormone-depleted serum, by PPARα knockdown)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in medium containing thyroid hormone-depleted serum. Increased by the addition of T3 in an almost dose-dependent manner. Partially but significantly suppressed in T3-treated cells following siRNA knockdown of PPARα. CPT1A protein levels were suppressed by PPARα knockdown.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Catalyzes the rate-limiting step of fatty acid conversion to acyl-CoA, necessary for fatty acid transport into mitochondria for subsequent beta-oxidation (liver isoform).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: T3 treatment in HepG2 cells; PPARα knockdown in T3-treated HepG2 cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Its expression is regulated by thyroid hormone and PPARα, indicating control over fatty acid beta-oxidation in the liver.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: T3 did not elevate expression levels of the CPT1B gene.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Skeletal muscle isoform of CPT1, involved in fatty acid transport into mitochondria for β-oxidation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: T3 treatment in human skeletal myotubular cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates that T3 does not directly regulate CPT1B expression in skeletal muscle, suggesting tissue-specific regulatory mechanisms for fatty acid beta-oxidation.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Gamma Coactivator-1 Alpha (PGC1α) gene

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: T3 could increase the expression level of PGC1α gene. Upregulation by T3 was independent of the PPARα pathway.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates expression of a broad range of genes involved in energy metabolism, including oxidative phosphorylation; its expression is regulated by thyroid hormones.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: T3 treatment in human skeletal myotubular cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Its upregulation by T3 in skeletal muscle enhances mitochondrial basal respiration and ATP production, indicating improved energy metabolism.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Mitochondrial basal respiration and ATP production

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: T3 significantly enhanced mitochondrial basal respiration and ATP production measured by an extracellular flux analyzer.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Fundamental processes of cellular energy production.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: T3 treatment in human skeletal myotubular cells, consistent with the function of PGC1α.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved cellular energy metabolism and function in response to T3 in skeletal muscle.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Blood pressure responses to Valsalva maneuver

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 100% of patients with PD with orthostatic hypotension (OH) had abnormal blood pressure responses. 26.1% of patients with PD without OH had abnormal Valsalva responses.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures the integrity of the autonomic nervous system, particularly sympathetic innervation controlling blood pressure.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Patients with Parkinson's Disease, with and without orthostatic hypotension (OH).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Abnormal responses indicate sympathetic dysfunction and contribute to orthostatic hypotension in PD patients.
